newsitem.title: ITALY: EMU delay risky for Italy - industry leader.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay risky for Italy - industry leader.

text.p: A delay in the launch of European economic and monetary union would be risky for Italy because the government might ease its efforts to sort out public finances, the President of the employers' federation Confindustria said.
Giorgio Fossa told reporters that he knew nothing of reports that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmayer had asked whether Germany and France could consider delaying EMU's launch.

"I don't know anything about this but what is certain is that a delay in EMU risks easing the tension (in government efforts to sort out state finances)," Fossa told reporters while attending the Bank of Italy's annual assembly.
"The winds of the (financial) markets risk breaking the weak links and one of these weak links is Italy," said Fossa.

The government has imposed a heavy tax squeeze in a bid to lower the ratio of the public sector deficit to gross domestic product to three percent this year -- a key requirement for joining a monetary union planned for 1999. Rome newsroom +396-6782505
